title: Soup Servings
summary: You start with two soups, A and B, each containing n mL.
statement: You start with two soups, A and B, each containing n mL. On each turn, one of four serving operations is chosen randomly, each with a probability of 0.25: pouring 100 mL from A and 0 mL from B, pouring 75 mL from A and 25 mL from B, pouring 50 mL from A and 50 mL from B, or pouring 25 mL from A and 75 mL from B. If an operation requests more than the available amount, only the available amount is poured. The process stops when one of the soups is used up. Calculate the probability that soup A is used up before soup B, plus half the probability that both soups are used up in the same turn. Results within 10^-5 of the correct answer are acceptable.
constraints: Initially each soup has n ml; four equally likely operations serve multiples of 25 ml.
Return P(A empties first)+0.5*P(both empty together), within 1e-5.
hints: Serving amounts share a factor of 25, so rounded units preserve every state transition.
Memoize probabilities for remaining unit pairs and shortcut the converged large-n tail.
Apply four transitions; base cases return 1, 0, or 0.5 depending on which soup empties.
The recurrence conditions on the next equally likely operation and terminates as at least one amount decreases.
editorial: The recurrence conditions on the next equally likely operation and terminates as at least one amount decreases.

tests.explanation: The four first operations contribute outcomes 1, 1, 1, and one half, averaging 0.625.
Both soups start empty, contributing one half.
